problem: Long prompts, outputs and concurrency exhaust memory or latency budgets.
principle: Measure prefill, decode and queues separately. KV caching, batching and quantization involve workload-specific tradeoffs.
check: Is more throughput with worse p95 first-token latency a success?
answer: Only if it meets the workload SLO. Interactive latency and offline throughput are separate objectives.

procedures.state: Layer K/V, positions, length and cache ownership.
procedures.failure: Do not mix models/prefixes/access scopes; long context still costs memory.
procedures.measure: First-token latency, token time and KV bytes.
procedures.case: The stated 32-layer example needs about 512 MiB of KV, excluding other memory.

procedures.state: Lengths, KV block tables, queues and limits.
procedures.failure: Do not trade unbounded queues for throughput.
procedures.measure: Throughput and p95 at equal arrival rates.
procedures.case: vLLM-style scheduling/cache management still needs workload SLO tests.

procedures.failure: Fall back on unsupported kernels or regressions; do not blindly repeat OOMs.
procedures.measure: Quality, latency and peak memory under fixed loads.
procedures.case: Fitting weights alone does not establish long-context concurrency capacity.
